name: Orion VC
identity_check: Confirmed as Orion VC (orionvc.co; the page metadata also points to orionvc.uk), a pre-seed AI fund run by Sergey Dean and Armen Fljyan. Its site lists 'Immigrant founders' and 'Building in the US' among its approach points, which matches the One Way Summit lead. Its Substack (orionvc.substack.com, linked from the site) carries the portfolio posts. Its LinkedIn company page (linked from the site) names orionvc.co, San Francisco and a 2024 founding. Ruled out: orionvc.com (a parked domain for sale); Orion Venture Partners / Orion Opportunity Fund (a separate Palo Alto / Taipei investor); Orion Worldwide Innovations (an Armenian startup accelerator); Orion Security (an Israeli startup, not an investor); and the other immigrant-founder funds One Way Ventures, Unshackled Ventures and Geek Ventures.

thesis_text.value: Pre-seed fund backing deeply technical founders in AI infrastructure, physical AI and vertical AI, favouring hard-to-build markets with high barriers to entry. It explicitly seeks immigrant founders and teams building in the US, backs the founder over the idea, and looks for moats from proprietary data, reinforcement learning and real-world deployment feedback.

open_items: Only 2 rounds could be documented, short of the 8 Tier A target. The Jan 2026 '2025 in review' post reports four portfolio companies, all backed in stealth. It says Orion led two rounds and that one physical-AI company won a $900K grant, but no fetched page names the other three. Dealroom, Crunchbase and village.ai returned 403, the Wayback Machine was offline, and content.orionvc.co and www.orionvc.co/about-us (a search hit) did not resolve.

No fund vehicle, fund size or close date published. The 2025 review thanks LPs, and the Data Moats post invites people to join as a 'fund LP', so the fund may still be raising. SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so Form D was not checked.
No check size stated. The Org shows only placeholders ('$xxxk' upfront, up to '$xM' follow-on).

No application form or pitch URL. The site's Contact section gives an email (not recorded), the LinkedIn page and a Substack newsletter. Cold inbound is taken from 'If you are building in this space, we want to hear from you.'

Indian founders: the site backs immigrant founders in general but never mentions India or Indian founders, so this is 'unknown'. The site describes no help with relocation, visas or US incorporation; it only says it backs founders 'building in the US'.

US entity: 'Building in the US' suggests US-based teams but states no entity requirement. Positronic Robotics, a 2026 investment, tests in Cyprus with a Paphos-based founder per Cyprus Mail; its incorporation was not checked.

Feedback Intelligence: the date is inferred. The Mar 2026 newsletter calls it Orion's first investment, made less than a year before the February 2026 ActiveCampaign acquisition, and the 2025 review covers the 2025 portfolio. No round size or co-investors are published. VCBacked (database) lists it in Berkeley, US, with a Mar 2023 $900K pre-seed (BANA Angels). CB Insights lists Hustle Fund, Berkeley SkyDeck and SmartGateVC as investors without round detail. Orion's 'backed in stealth' wording does not obviously fit a company with public rounds since 2022.
portfolio_count_reported (4) dates from Jan 2026, before the Sept 2026 Positronic investment.

Other team members not recorded as partners: 'Martin, IR Partner' (surname not given, 2025 review) and Arseniy Gurin, Associate (The Org, database only). Partner focus_sectors are classified from site bios and posts; the firm does not assign sectors.
Attendance at One Way Summit SF 2026 was not confirmed on any fetched page. The 'Immigrant founders' focus in the lead does match the firm's own site.
